1: # Persist custom chord sequences in SQLite and match them at runtime
2: 
3: The app shipped with six "famous sequence" presets hardcoded in `main.py` and a
4: `SEQ_FAMOSA` tag precomputed into the CSV at scrape time. The frontend hardcoded
5: four of those six. There was no way for a visitor to add a sequence, and no code
6: path that compared a user-supplied sequence against a song's chords: the runtime
7: check was a membership test against the precomputed tag. The custom-sequences
8: feature requires an anonymous catalog that survives container restarts and grows
9: without a new deploy.
10: 
11: We are introducing a single SQLite database, created with the `sqlite3` module
12: already present in the `python:3.9-slim` image, holding only the sequence
13: catalog. Songs and genres stay in `data/top/dataset_final.csv`, loaded into
14: memory at startup as before, because the task explicitly keeps that boundary.
15: The database lives at `/app/instance/sequences.db`, outside `/app/data` — a bind
16: mount over `/app/data` would hide the 15.8 MB CSV that `Dockerfile:8` copies
17: into the image. The `Dockerfile` declares `VOLUME /app/instance`, and the README
18: and AGENTS.md document `docker run -p 8080:8080 -v ciframe-data:/app/instance
19: ciframe`; without the named volume the file survives `docker restart` but is
20: lost when the container is recreated. We chose SQLite over Postgres or Redis
21: because a second service contradicts ADR 0001's single-container, local-only
22: deploy, over in-memory state because that fails the persistence requirement, and
23: over `shelve`/JSON files because SQLite is transactional, already available, and
24: inspectable with SQL without adding a dependency.
25: 
26: For matching, we are replacing the tag lookup with a runtime function that
27: implements the tag's exact semantics: the catalog sequence must appear as a
28: contiguous block of tokens in the song's ordered chord list, and every chord in
29: the song must belong to the sequence's vocabulary, comparing only lowercased
30: strings. The research validated this definition against all 67,585 loaded songs:
31: it reproduces the six original result sets exactly (199, 296, 4, 5, 7, 3 songs)
32: with zero extra and zero missing IDs, which is the feature's regression
33: criterion. Looser definitions (contiguous without the closed vocabulary, ordered
34: subsequence, or set intersection) return thousands of additional songs and would
35: break that criterion; a dual-mode catalog would preserve the six but give the
36: same search two different meanings, which is why it was rejected. The
37: consequence we accept is that a user-created sequence can return very few or no
38: songs: a single passing chord outside the sequence disqualifies a song. The UI
39: states the rule instead of hiding it.
40: 
41: Because matching no longer reads `SEQ_FAMOSA`, `Musica` drops `seqs_famosas` and
42: the CSV loader stops splitting column 7. The column and
43: `scripts/generate_data_set.py` remain untouched: the tag is still the oracle for
44: the regression test in `scripts/validar_matching.py`, comparing sets of
45: `id_unico_musica` rather than counts. The six originals are seeded into the
46: catalog idempotently and keep their old keys (`BmGDA`, `CGAmF`, ...) so existing
47: `GET /similares?sequencia=` URLs keep working; new and old sequences are searched
48: through `sequencia_id`. Duplicate registration by canonical chord list returns
49: the existing row with HTTP 201 instead of creating a second entry, and result
50: ordering and pagination remain exactly as they are today.
51: 
52: This decision has deliberate limits. The catalog is open and anonymous: there is
53: no login, moderation, or rate limiting, and spam is an accepted risk for this
54: iteration. Matching scans the in-memory song list once per request, as the
55: sequence path already did, now comparing chord lists instead of tags; if latency
56: degrades as the catalog or traffic grows, a precomputed index can be added
57: without changing the semantics. If the product later needs higher recall for
58: custom sequences, loosening the closed-vocabulary condition is a new decision
59: that must be recorded separately, because it necessarily changes what the six
60: original sequences return.

   - `POST /sequencias`: exigir JSON com `acordes` não vazio, no máximo 32 itens
     de 1 a 20 caracteres após `strip`, sem `;`; nome opcional com até 80
     caracteres e derivado de `A - B - C` quando ausente. Canonicalizar somente
     com `strip` + `lower`.
   - Duplicata por `chords_norm` devolve a linha existente com HTTP 201, sem

   - Em `GET /similares`, aceitar `sequencia_id=<int>`: id inválido ou

## Riscos e mitigação

| Risco | Como perceber | O que fazer |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline capturado com dataset, porta ou imagem diferente | Totais diferentes de `199, 296, 4, 5, 7, 3` ou hash do CSV diferente | Parar antes de codar; conferir `docker build`, `GET /generos`, caminho do CSV e hash; recapturar |
| Ordem dos resultados mudar no refactor | Comparador acusa divergência apenas de ordem | Não ordenar para “consertar”; revisar iteração de `musicas.values()`, `apply_filtro` e `get_pagina` |
| Remoção da tag quebrar o caminho legado | Comparador falha logo após o passo 4 | Fazer seed + lookup por `legacy_key` + matcher no mesmo passo; manter o `replace(',', '')` |
| SQLite bloqueado ou perdido | `database is locked` ou catálogo vazio após recriar o container | `busy_timeout`, conexão por operação, 1 worker e teste real com volume nomeado |
| Validação divergir do contrato (duplicata, limites) | Testes de API falham no 201/400 | Seguir a proposta: normalizar só `strip`+`lower`, duplicata devolve a linha existente |
| Frontend antigo em cache ou erro silencioso no AngularJS | Browser não lista o catálogo ou mostra 4 sequências | Hard reload, console do browser e conferir inclusão de scripts em `index.html` |
| Cadastro anônimo virar depósito de spam | Catálogo com entradas inúteis | Risco aceito nesta iteração; não implementar login/rate limit/moderação sem nova decisão |
| Escopo crescer para músicas/gêneros no banco ou normalização de acordes | Diff toca `data/`, `generate_data_set.py` ou regras além de `lower()` | Reverter; essas mudanças estão explicitamente fora do escopo |

      controle passando contra o código antigo.

      `id_unico_musica`, na mesma ordem, que o baseline: `199, 296, 4, 5, 7, 3`.
- [ ] `GET /similares?sequencia_id=<id>` funciona para as 6 originais e para
      sequências novas, com paginação de 100 e filtro de gênero.
- [ ] `GET /sequencias` lista as 6 originais primeiro e todas as novas.
- [ ] `POST /sequencias` cria (`201`), deduplica (`201` com a linha existente) e
      rejeita entrada inválida (`400`); uma sequência nova cadastrada é
      encontrável pela busca.
- [ ] Sequência nova persiste após `docker restart` e após `docker rm` + novo
      `docker run` com o mesmo volume nomeado.
- [ ] `#/porsequencia` mostra as 6 + novas, cadastra sequência ordenada, busca
      por `id`, pagina com “carregar mais”, usa os 52 gêneros do backend e
      explica o estado vazio.
- [ ] `seqs_famosas` não é mais usado em runtime; a coluna `SEQ_FAMOSA` e o CSV
      continuam intactos apenas como oráculo de teste.
- [ ] `scripts/validar_matching.py` continua mostrando a regra E idêntica à tag
      nas 6 sequências, e a suíte `unittest` passa.
- [ ] Endpoints continuam devolvendo `json.dumps` como `text/html` e mantendo
      CORS `*`; nenhum endpoint fora do escopo mudou.
- [ ] `04-test-report.md` preenchido com cobertura, comandos e resultado da
      regressão.
